speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please tell me how far along you are in your pregnancy and describe the severity and location of the abdominal pain you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your previous cesarean section and the sudden onset of severe pain with bleeding, I need to check the fetal status immediately. I will also examine your abdomen to see if it is rigid or tender. REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring

speaker: Doctor
text: The recurrent variable decelerations indicate fetal distress, which is concerning given your history of a prior cesarean section and current symptoms. I need to assess the integrity of your uterine scar immediately. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Exam_Uterus

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No contractions felt at the time of examination

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of contractions combined with severe pain and fetal distress strongly suggests uterine rupture. I need to confirm the diagnosis and assess for internal hemorrhage immediately. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound findings of uterine wall disruption and hemoperitoneum, combined with your history and symptoms, confirm a uterine rupture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
